entry.title: PyTorch Frustratometer: An Ultra-fast, Parallelized Tool for Proteome-Scale Local Energetic Frustration Analysis
entry.summary:
Most natural protein sequences fold into well-defined three-dimensional structural ensembles, satisfying interactions that have been shaped over evolutionary timescales. The principle of minimal frustration states that most native interactions are energetically more favorable than alternative non-native ones, resulting in a funnel-shaped folding energy landscape. The FrustratometeR tool measures how the energetics of a residue or contact compares to decoys with different amino acid identities or configurations.

Source: bioRxiv Bioinformatics Preprints · Tags: #bioinformatics #genomics-proteins #rust

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: KORD: Breaking the Key-Generation Bottleneck in Dealerless Function Secret Sharing via Protocol–Hardware Co-Design
entry.summary:
Function secret sharing (FSS) has emerged as a promising technique for secure multi-party computation (MPC), offering a lightweight online phase. However, existing FSS-based private inference frameworks typically rely on trusted dealers to generate and distribute large amounts of offline key material (e.g., 16.8 GiB for BERT-base), incurring substantial overhead in key generation, transfer, storage, and parsing. Cryptographic dealer-free FSS eliminates the trusted dealer but introduces costly interaction during key generation.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #combinatorics

entry.title: Financial Advisors and Retirees' Risk-taking -- by Allison T. Cole, Maarten Meeuwis, Alessandro Previtero, Noah Stoffman
entry.summary:
Advised retirees keep about two-thirds of their portfolios in equities well into old age—30 to 40 percentage points more than non-advised retirees, target-date funds, or common rules of thumb. These allocations reflect active choices rather than inertia, and they adjust gradually toward a new advisor’s investment style following advisor switches. Equity shares rise with relationship tenure, and advisor influence is strongest among clients with low financial knowledge or risk tolerance, consistent with trust facilitating risk-taking.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #rust
